 4 weather alerts in effect TSA expects Thanksgiving travel rush at Las Vegas airport 
 TSA expects busy Las Vegas airport security lines after Formula 1 and during Thanksgiving week. 
 By Brittany Defran Published : Nov. 18, 2026 at 4:10 PM PST | Updated : 2 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google LAS VEGAS ( FOX5 ) — Travelers flying through Harry Reid International Airport should prepare for busy security checkpoints during the Thanksgiving holiday period, the Transportation Security Administration said.
 The agency expects the busiest local travel days to include the Tuesday and Wednesday before Thanksgiving, as well as Sunday, Nov. 29, and Monday, Nov. 30. TSA spokesperson Daniel Velez said the airport also expects a surge on Sunday, Nov. 22, as visitors leave Las Vegas after the Formula 1 race.
 “So, it’s going to be very busy here the next couple of weeks,” Velez said.
 TSA recommends arriving at least two hours before a domestic flight and three hours before an international flight. Travelers should allow extra time for parking, airline check-in, baggage drop, and security screening. Velez suggested that families traveling with children consider arriving even earlier.
 Passengers should have an acceptable ID ready at the checkpoint, Velez said. Acceptable identification includes a REAL ID, a passport, an enhanced driver’s license or a military ID, he said.
 MORE ON FOX5: Mullin faces questions from Congress over flight disruptions, football trip and immigration 
 Thanksgiving food and airport security 
 Travelers can bring solid foods such as pies, turkey, stuffing, casseroles and fresh produce in carry-on bags, according to TSA. Liquid or spreadable foods over 3.4 ounces, including gravy, cranberry sauce and preserves, should go in checked luggage.
 “If you can spill it, spray it, spread it, pump it, or pour it, and it’s more than 3.4 ounces, it needs to go in your checked bag,” Velez said.
 Ice packs used to keep food cold must be completely frozen when passengers reach security, TSA said. Travelers can check specific items using the “What Can I Bring?” feature in the myTSA app or contact @AskTSA on X, Facebook Messenger or by texting “Travel” to 275-872.
 Screening technology at Harry Reid 
 TSA said the airport uses technology that verifies travelers’ identities, automated screening lanes and computed tomography scanners that produce 3D images of carry-on bags. At lanes equipped with CT scanners, passengers in standard screening can leave laptops, other electronics, and compliant liquids in their bags, the agency said.
 Eligible TSA PreCheck passengers can also opt in to Touchless ID at participating checkpoints, according to the agency.
 TSA said it expects to release national Thanksgiving travel projections later this week. Early indicators suggest it could screen more than 3 million passengers nationwide on Sunday, Nov. 29.
